dakshinamurthy.name: Dakshinamurthy
dakshinamurthy.description: Shiva depicted as the supreme teacher, seated facing south, teaching sages in silence.
dakshinamurthy.significance: Represents the transmission of knowledge beyond words.
dakshinamurthy.mythology: Associated with Shiva imparting wisdom to rishis under a banyan tree.

Dancing_Shiva.name: Nataraja (Dancing Shiva)
Dancing_Shiva.description: Shiva performing the cosmic dance, often shown with multiple arms in dynamic motion.
Dancing_Shiva.significance: Symbolizes the cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction.
Dancing_Shiva.mythology: The Ananda Tandava dance, performed to destroy a demon and restore cosmic order.

durga.name: Durga
durga.description: The warrior goddess, often depicted with multiple arms holding weapons.
durga.significance: Represents the triumph of good over evil and divine feminine power.
durga.mythology: Known for slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

nandi.name: Nandi
nandi.description: The bull, Shiva's mount and gatekeeper, usually seated facing the sanctum.
nandi.mythology: Nandi guards the entrance to Shiva's abode and is worshipped as his devoted attendant.

Shiva_Parvati.name: Shiva-Parvati
Shiva_Parvati.description: Shiva and Parvati depicted together, often in an intimate or domestic pose.
Shiva_Parvati.significance: Represents the union of masculine and feminine cosmic principles.
Shiva_Parvati.mythology: Parvati is Shiva's consort, and their union represents wholeness in Hindu cosmology.
